# enterprise-shift: the stewards work their tickets

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

One shift of the enterprise: the engine that takes open tickets from [`data/enterprise/tickets/`](../../../../../data/enterprise/tickets/README.md), works each through the [program workflow](../../../../../packages/improvement/program/README.md) in its own git worktree and session, has an independent reviewer decide on the result, assembles the approved changes onto the development branch, recertifies them there, and pushes them with the shift's ledger lines and record. [`driver.ts`](driver.ts) is the engine, [`shift.ts`](shift.ts) its pure half, and `pnpm run enterprise -- shift` ([`scripts/enterprise.ts`](../../../../../scripts/enterprise.ts)) the command that launches one shift on the operator's Claude Code route. The [Agent Note](../../../../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-28-enterprise-shift-engine.md) records the decisions.

## What one shift does

1. **Clone.** `git clone --branch <branch> --single-branch` of the remote into `<scratch>/repo`, borrowing objects from the local repository when git can (`--reference-if-able`; a shallow local repository lends none, and the clone then fetches everything). The tip it was cut at is the base revision of every worktree; `remote.origin.pushurl` is set to an unreachable value, so a department that pushes through `origin` reaches nothing.
2. **Select.** The clone's queue is read and validated ([`scripts/enterprise-tickets.ts`](../../../../../scripts/enterprise-tickets.ts)); its `data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl` closes a ticket whose latest line was shipped or rejected by review; `--next <n>` takes the first `n` open tickets in queue order (fewest attempts, a halt on the usage limit not counting as one; then priority; then each division in turn; then id), `--tickets <id,...>` the named ones.
3. **Program.** One program spec: one department per ticket (key `t-nnnn`, the ticket id lowered), the `implementing` preset, the ticket's budget as its caps, and a standard of the ticket's acceptance commands followed by the engine's checks — `engine-committed` (the branch carries a commit past the base), `engine-scope` (`git diff --name-only` with every scope prefix excluded lists nothing), `engine-whitespace` (`git diff --check`) and, for a queue whose policy names a documentation gate (this repository's names `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing`), `engine-documentation`, which runs that gate whenever the diff touches a Markdown document and passes without it otherwise; the integration and the recertification run the same gate over the merged and the assembled change. The objective names the ticket, the seat from the roster, the task, the scope, the acceptance commands, and points the department at `CLAUDE.md` and the package README. Every worktree is added and installed offline (`pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile`, when the repository has a lockfile) before the program starts, so the acceptance commands find an installed workspace. The program's own integration merges every certified department and repeats every ticket's acceptance over the merged head.
4. **Review.** Each certified department is reviewed in a session that never saw it: a fresh id with no parent and no seed, the `reviewing` preset (`role: judge`), every global tool restricted away (`tools.restrict({ allow: [] })`, because the deployment's tools are global rows and a reviewer with a shell could read the department's worktree), an empty working directory of its own under `<scratch>/review/`, and three messages — the standing instruction, the ticket, and the evidence (`git diff <base> <revision>`, the messages of the branch's commits, and every check's output, each bounded). The answer's first `verdict: approve|reject` line decides; an answer naming neither rejects.
5. **Assemble.** Approved departments are squashed onto the base in ticket order, one commit per ticket, authored and committed as `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` (the clone's `user.name` and `user.email`, which the department commits share), whose message names the shift (`Shift: Daliesk shift <id>`), the ticket, the seat, the program id, both sessions, and ends with `Co-Authored-By: <the department's model>` and the `Claude-Session:` line. The engine's own commits pass `--no-verify`: the change was certified by the ticket's acceptance, and the clone's git hooks are the contributor's, installed for the departments by the offline install. When every department was approved, the assembled tree must equal the program's certified merged tree; every assembled ticket's acceptance then runs again over the assembled tree in the clone's own checkout. A squash that conflicts, a digest that differs, or an acceptance that fails ships nothing and records why.
6. **Ship.** The ledger lines and the record are committed after the assembled commits. With `--push`, the remote tip is fetched: when it moved, the assembled commits are rebased onto it, recertified there, and the ledger rewritten around their new hashes; a rebase that conflicts ships nothing and still pushes the ledger. The push is one fast-forward update of the branch, tried up to three rounds while the tip keeps moving. A shift that ships nothing still pushes its ledger lines and record.
7. **Halt.** The first `turn/end` whose failure carries the LLM seam's `QUOTA` code — the route's usage-limit notice as [the seam classifies it](../../../../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-09-27-route-limit-halts-the-run.md) — blocks that department's goal with `route-limit`, so its attempt ends without a validation run; every later department blocks on its first refused turn; nothing is reviewed, assembled, or shipped; every unfinished ticket's line reads `halted: limit (resets at <instant>)`; the driver exits 3.

## The ledger and the record

`data/enterprise/ledger.jsonl` gains one line per ticket per shift: `{ type: "ticket", at, shift, ticket, seat, division, programId, implementer, model, department: { outcome, sessionId }, checks: [{ id, ok }], review: { verdict, sessionId }, integration: { outcome }, shipped: { commit } | null, reason, tokens, seconds }`. `department.outcome` is `certified`, `failed`, `blocked`, `abandoned`, `pending` or `halted`; `review.verdict` is `approve`, `reject` or `none`; `integration.outcome` is `merged`, `skipped`, `conflict`, `checks-failed`, `digest-mismatch` or `not-shipped`. A ticket is closed once its latest line is shipped or rejected; any other line leaves it open for a later shift. The engine reads only ticket lines: a line without `type` counts as one, and a line of any other `type` — the enterprise functions' `function` lines share the file — is skipped.

`data/enterprise/shifts/<UTC date>-<shift id>/` holds `result.json` (the shift, the program report, every ticket's line with the reviewer's rationale, the halt), `manifest.json` (the base, the branch, the composition, every file's SHA-256) and `sessions/<session id>.jsonl` for every session of the shift — the program ledger, each department, each review, the integration. Credential-shaped strings are cut from every recorded byte and counted in `result.json`.

## The two compositions

[`cordis.yml`](cordis.yml) is the keyless half: every session runs on the `cli-mock` route of [`enterprise-llm.ts`](enterprise-llm.ts), whose departments are scripted per ticket of [`seed/`](seed/): `T-0001` delivers, `T-0002` delivers the wrong output, `T-0003` delivers and is rejected by the scripted reviewer, `T-0004` also writes outside its scope, `T-0005` moves the remote tip before it commits; `DSH_TEST_ENTERPRISE_LIMIT=1` makes every department turn fail with the `QUOTA` code and a stated reset. [`overlays/claude-code.cordis.yml`](overlays/claude-code.cordis.yml) is the real one: the scripted route disabled, the operator's Claude Code installation inserted, `DSH_ENTERPRISE_MODEL` (default `sonnet`) as every session's model, and the subagent seam composed so that `--implementer subagent` can delegate each department to Claude Code itself.

## Running it keyless

```sh
pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.e2e.config.ts examples/headless-agent/tests/enterprise-shift.e2e.ts
```

[`enterprise-shift.e2e.ts`](../../enterprise-shift.e2e.ts) seeds a bare remote from `seed/` and runs four shifts against it: `T-0001,T-0002,T-0004` (one ticket ships, one fails its acceptance, one fails the scope check; the remote gains the ticket commit and the shift commit), `T-0003` (certified, rejected, not shipped, closed in the ledger), `T-0005` (the tip moves, the shift rebases, recertifies and ships) and the limit halt over two tickets. [`enterprise-shift.spec.ts`](../../enterprise-shift.spec.ts) covers selection, the compiled standard, the verdict line, the commit message and the redaction; [`scripts/enterprise.spec.ts`](../../../../../scripts/enterprise.spec.ts) the command line, the lock and the sweep.

## Running it for real

```sh
DSH_ENTERPRISE_SCRATCH=/path/outside/the/repository pnpm run enterprise -- shift --next 2 --push
```

The command needs the `claude` CLI installed and logged in, an installed workspace (the clone installs offline from the same store), and push access to `origin`. `--tickets <id,...>` names tickets instead of `--next`, `--implementer subagent` delegates departments to Claude Code, `--model <id>` picks the product model, `--branch <name>` another branch than the development branch, `--keep` keeps the clone, and `--composition <path>` another composition. The wrapper writes `<scratch>/<shift id>/run.log` and the driver's session logs under `<scratch>/<shift id>/.sessions/`; a clone whose push failed is kept and named on stderr, every other clone is removed when the shift ends, and clones a day old are swept when the next shift starts.

The command is safe for an unattended schedule. `<scratch>/shift.lock` names the running shift's pid; a second shift refuses to start while that pid is alive (exit 4) and replaces the lock of a shift that died. Nothing reaches the remote before the one push at the end, so an interrupted shift leaves the branch as it found it and its next run selects from the ledger the branch carries. Exit codes: 0 for a shift that ran to its end (whether or not it shipped), 2 when the push failed in every round, 3 for a halt at the route limit, 4 for a shift refused by the lock.
